items.question: What cleansing action must follow the offering of arghya water?
premises: Arghya water has been given
Clay is taken for cleansing
Both feet require washing afterward
items.inference: After giving arghya, one should take clay and wash the feet.
items.plain_english: After giving the water offering, one should take clay and then wash the feet.

items.question: What purification and entry steps follow the washing of the feet?
premises: Mouth-rinsing is done with water
The performer becomes purified by rinsing
The guests are then led inside
items.inference: After washing, one performs mouth-rinsing and then leads the guests in.
items.plain_english: Afterwards, one should perform mouth-rinsing with water, and having rinsed, lead them in.

items.question: Where and how should the invited guests be seated after entry?
premises: Seats have been well washed
The guests are recognized and present
The officiant must seat them properly
items.inference: The guests should be seated on well-washed seats.
items.plain_english: Recognizing them, one should seat them on seats that have been well washed.

items.question: What seating material must be given to the two recipients after permission?
premises: Permission is granted with the word kuruṣva
Two recipients are involved
A darbha seat is to be offered
items.inference: After being permitted, one should give a darbha seat to the two.
items.plain_english: Having been permitted with the words 'do so,' one should give a darbha-grass seat to the two.

items.question: How must the upper garment be arranged while placing the north-pointed seat?
premises: The seat is oriented northward
The Sadyojāta mantra is used
The upper garment is placed on the left
items.inference: One places the north-pointed seat with the Sadyojāta mantra while arranging the upper garment on the left.
uncertainties: ajātena interpreted as the Sadyojāta mantra by tradition
items.plain_english: Placing the north-pointed seat with the Sadyojāta mantra, one should arrange the upper garment on the left.

items.question: By what form of address must the officiant invite the guests after permission?
premises: Permission is given to invite
The invitation uses the guest's own name
The name begins with the praṇava
items.inference: After permission, one should invite using the guest's own name prefixed by om.
items.plain_english: Having been permitted with the word 'invite,' one should invoke them by their own name beginning with om.

items.question: What protective substance must be scattered around the ritual area next?
premises: Protection is required at this stage
Barley grains are taken
They are scattered around
items.inference: For protection, one should take barley grains and scatter them around.
items.plain_english: Then, for protection, one should take barley grains and scatter them all around.

items.question: How many times must the presence of the pair be invoked with the rūpi mantra?
premises: The rūpi mantra is employed
The goal is the presence of the pair
The action is done once for each
items.inference: Using the rūpi mantra, one invokes the presence of the pair once each.
uncertainties: rūpiṇā taken as a mantra name following tradition
items.plain_english: With the rūpi mantra, for the presence of the pair, one should do so once and once.

premises: The worshipper kneels on the ground
The Aghora mantra is used
Barley grains are the offering
items.inference: Kneeling on the ground, one should worship with barley using the Aghora mantra.
items.plain_english: Kneeling on the ground, one should worship with barley grains using the Aghora mantra.

items.question: How should the entire body be anointed and adorned during the worship?
premises: Scents are applied to the body
All limbs are anointed
Flower garlands are used for adornment
items.inference: One should anoint all limbs with scents and adorn them with flower garlands.
items.plain_english: Having anointed all the limbs with scents, one should adorn them with flower garlands.

items.question: Which mantra governs the placement of the lamp and the purifier?
premises: A lamp is to be placed
A purifier is also offered
The Īśāna mantra is specified
items.inference: One should place the lamp and the purifier with the Īśāna mantra.
items.plain_english: And one should place the lamp and the purifier with the Īśāna mantra.

items.question: In what manner must another related item be given at this stage?
premises: Another part or item is to be given
The manner follows the sacred-thread order
The giving is a prescribed step
items.inference: One should give another related item in the sacred-thread order.
uncertainties: tadaṅgam interpreted as another part of the purifier or offering
items.plain_english: Then one should give another part of it in the manner of the sacred thread.

items.question: How must the kuśa grasses be offered using the Sadyojāta mantra?
premises: Kuśa grasses are to be given
They are given twofold
The Sadyojāta mantra is recited
items.inference: One should give twofold kuśa grasses with the Sadyojāta mantra.
items.plain_english: Having given twofold kuśa grasses, one should do so with the Sadyojāta mantra.

items.question: In what direction and with which mantra must the threefold establishment be performed?
premises: A triad beginning with establishment is performed
The Vāma mantra is used
The movement is counter-clockwise
items.inference: One should perform the threefold act beginning with establishment counter-clockwise with the Vāma mantra.
items.plain_english: Having performed the three acts beginning with establishment, one should do so counter-clockwise with the Vāma mantra.

items.question: How must the presence of the three be invoked separately with the Aghora mantra?
premises: The presence of three is sought
The Aghora mantra is employed
The act is done separately in the palms
items.inference: For the presence of the three, one should act separately in the palms with the Aghora mantra.
items.plain_english: For the presence of the three, one should do so separately in the joined palms with the Aghora mantra.

items.question: From what point and in what posture must the sequence proceed with the Īśa mantra?
premises: One knee rests on the ground
The Īśa mantra is used
The sequence proceeds from the head in order
items.inference: With one knee on the ground and the Īśa mantra, one proceeds in order beginning from the head.
items.plain_english: With one knee on the ground, using the Īśa mantra, one should proceed in order beginning from the head.

items.question: Which offerings must be presented next using the rūpi mantra?
premises: Scents and related items are offered
Incense and lamp are included
The rūpi mantra governs the offering
items.inference: Then one should have scents and so on, along with incense and lamp, offered with the rūpi mantra.
uncertainties: rūpiṇā taken as a mantra name following tradition
items.plain_english: Then one should cause offerings beginning with scents, and incense and lamp, to be given with the rūpi mantra.

items.question: What reciprocal declaration of fullness must be spoken by both parties?
premises: The officiant must say 'let it be full'
The recipients must respond likewise
The utterance affirms completeness
items.inference: The officiant should say 'let it be full,' and they too should say 'let it be full.'
items.plain_english: One should say, 'May it be full,' and they too should say, 'May it be full.'

items.question: How must the vessel designated as the ancestors' place be positioned?
premises: The vessel is identified as the ancestors' place
It is to be inverted
It is placed downward
items.inference: Saying 'you are the place of the ancestors,' one should place the vessel inverted and downward.
items.plain_english: Saying, 'You are the place of the ancestors,' one should place the vessel inverted, facing downward.

items.question: What kind of vessel must be provided for serving the food?
premises: A vessel is taken for serving
The vessel must be pure
It is provided for food
items.inference: One should take a pure vessel and provide it for the food.

items.question: What protective measure must be taken to remove faults in the dining row?
premises: Faults in the row must be removed

items.plain_english: Then, to remove faults in the row, one should set out protective separators.

items.question: What permission must the officiant seek from the twice-born before the fire oblation?
premises: An oblation in the Śiva-fire is intended
The officiant declares intent to perform it
The twice-born must be asked for permission
items.inference: One should ask the twice-born, saying 'I will perform the oblation in the Śiva-fire.'
items.plain_english: One should ask the twice-born, saying, 'I will perform the oblation in the fire of Śiva.'

items.question: What mantra formula must be uttered when addressing Soma with the ancestors' epithet?
premises: Soma is addressed in the dative form
The word includes the epithet for ancestors
The formula ends with svadhā and namaḥ
items.inference: One should utter the dative formula to Soma with the ancestors' epithet, followed by svadhā and namaḥ.
items.plain_english: One should say the formula to Soma, with the word for 'accompanied by the ancestors' in the dative, followed by 'svadhā, homage.'

items.question: What mantra formula must follow when addressing Agni as the bearer of offerings?
premises: The previous formula has been uttered
Agni is addressed as kavyavāhana
The formula ends with svadhā and namaḥ
items.inference: After that, one should say the formula to Agni, the bearer of offerings, followed by svadhā and namaḥ.
items.plain_english: Having said that, one should then say to Agni, the bearer of offerings, 'svadhā, homage.'
